title: The hypertrophy series: programming strength work to bolster tonnage quality & progression
summary: NH defines strength work as the session-opening, highest-intensity work done with absolute intensity and present every day. It should be synergistic with the rest of the session, ideally a big compound lift, limited to 1-3 sets with one rep in reserve. It gives the highest-quality but minority share of tonnage, warms you up for what follows, and sets the baseline for judging later sets.
claims: Every training day should have a strength work component
For a bodybuilder strength and hypertrophy work are one and the same; strength work just means the higher-intensity sets that drive progression
Strength work always opens the session, when you are freshest and absolute intensity is intact; anywhere else it is not strength work
The strength lift should be synergistic with the rest of the day, with echoes of its movement pattern later, e.g. deadlifts preparing you for rows and hinges
Work after strength work needs little or no warm-up
Skipping strength work and going straight to back-off sets can make those sets feel worse, because heavy strength work primes you for the weight
After deadlift strength work at 470 lb, 400 lb feels like nothing
Strength work sets the baseline: compare later loads to it, and too large a discrepancy means you are outside relevant intensity windows and should stop
Strength work can use any lift, but big compound movements make the most sense because they warm up more muscle groups
NH is not dogmatic about the big three; curls, overhead press or heavy triceps extensions can be strength work
Physical and mental stamina rise during warm-up and ideally peak together; that peak is where strength work happens
Keep strength work to 1-3 sets, 4 at most; managing 5-6 sets means you are sandbagging
Strength work sets go to failure but carry the highest injury risk
NH leaves one rep in the tank on strength work: if his max is 5 reps on squat, he does 4 so every rep stays clean
NH never gambles with strength work; if he misses a planned rep it is a misgroove or poor recovery, not mis-programming
Reps in the tank make the most sense for natural bodybuilding longevity and muscle mass
Strength work yields the highest-quality tonnage but should be a minority of the session's total, like royal jelly in a hive's honey
Doing only strength work and stopping burned out accumulates far less tonnage than using it as an opener and finishing the session
If strength work leaves you burned out mentally or in your tendons, lower its intensity or modify the sets to train the rest of the session
Endurance and stamina decline through the session while tonnage keeps rising; where they cross is roughly where training should end
Choose strength lifts that branch into many variations: bench feeds all bench variations, a triceps extension carries over little
If you do six deadlift variations, the deadlift should be your strength work because it feeds them most
